# Ouijit

> Ouijit is a task and terminal manager for macOS and Linux for running coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode) in parallel. Each task gets its own git worktree and terminal, lifecycle hooks launch the agent CLI with the right context, and a session-aware CLI lets agents drive the board back. Live status, notifications, diff review, an experimental GitHub pull request surface, and per-terminal sandboxing (Seatbelt/Landlock via nono, or a launcher you supply) are built in.

Free and open source under the AGPL-3.0 license. No account, no sign-in. Distributed as a downloadable desktop app for macOS 13+ and Linux x64.

Every page below is also served as plain Markdown at https://ouijit.com/docs/<slug>.md (for example https://ouijit.com/docs/cli.md). The full docs in one file: https://ouijit.com/llms-full.txt

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://ouijit.com/docs/): Requirements, download links, building from source, adding projects, the projects folder, environment checks, updates.
- [Tasks and worktrees](https://ouijit.com/docs/worktrees/): The task board (columns, creating tasks, the task menu), per-task git worktrees, task lifecycle, the branch new tasks start from, merge targets, copy-on-write cloning, Quick start vs Clean checkout creation modes.
- [Terminals](https://ouijit.com/docs/terminals/): Sidebar of every project's tasks and terminals, card stack UI, keyboard shortcuts, terminal tags and the Tags view, resuming the last session (no hooks fire on resume).
- [Panels](https://ouijit.com/docs/panels/): Tabs on a terminal: runner (run hook and scripts), web preview (embedded browser), markdown with Mermaid and live reload. Multiple instances per kind; also opened via `ouijit markdown add` / `ouijit preview add`.
- [Command palette](https://ouijit.com/docs/palette/): Mod+K jump to terminals, projects, tasks, and pull requests, with often-used items ranked first; opening an unstarted task creates its worktree.
- [Diff review](https://ouijit.com/docs/diff/): Per-terminal worktree diff with a base picker (uncommitted, merge target, any branch), word-level highlighting, and notes that re-anchor as code moves and paste into the agent's prompt.
- [Pull requests and issues](https://ouijit.com/docs/pull-requests/): Experimental GitHub surface driven by the gh CLI: PR inbox, review comments staged locally until the user sends them, merging with optional admin bypass, an issues list from GitHub and Linear with search across both, linking tasks to pull requests and issues. Requires gh 2.48.0+ and `gh auth login`.
- [Sandbox](https://ouijit.com/docs/sandbox/): Run agents with permission checks off, limited to their task's worktree. A project Default (Host, Sandbox or Custom) that terminals, hooks, Run and scripts follow, overridden per hook, per run, from a task's Resume in menu, or for one command with `ouijit sandbox -- <command>`; an unavailable sandbox fails rather than falling back to the host. Ouijit's sandbox is nono (Seatbelt/Landlock) with a per-project profile file; Custom is a launcher you supply that owns the boundary. Ouijit CLI access inside a sandbox: read only, its own task, or everything.
- [Themes](https://ouijit.com/docs/themes/): System/light/dark, five presets (dracula, tokyo-night, matrix, hot-pink, sepia), custom design-token themes, `ouijit theme` CLI. Global, applies live, restyles terminals including the ANSI palette.
- [Hooks](https://ouijit.com/docs/hooks/): Four status hooks (start, continue, review, done) configured per project, each with its own Run in setting (Default, Host, Sandbox or Custom). Hooks receive OUIJIT_TASK_* env vars, including `OUIJIT_TASK_NUMBER`.
- [Supported agents](https://ouijit.com/docs/harnesses/): Status indicators and CLI awareness for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode via injected wrappers.
- [For agents](https://ouijit.com/docs/agents/): The contract for agents driving Ouijit: injected CLI reference, environment variables, headless hook flags, panel commands, the staged PR review workflow, sandbox constraints.
- [CLI](https://ouijit.com/docs/cli/): The `ouijit` command auto-installed in every terminal, with subcommands for tasks, terminals (list, read, open, paste, close), links that take the user somewhere in Ouijit, asking the user to run a command outside the sandbox, diff notes, hooks, scripts, runners, tags, chats, pull requests, themes, panels, projects, and the custom sandbox launcher.

## Project

- [Home](https://ouijit.com): Download links, demo, value prop.
- [Sandbox overview](https://ouijit.com/sandbox/): Why and how to run agents with permission checks off inside the sandbox; the docs page has the full contract.
- [Changelog](https://ouijit.com/changelog/): What changed in each release, rendered from the GitHub release notes.
- [About](https://ouijit.com/about/): Who builds Ouijit, and the commitments on price, privacy and licence.
- [FAQ](https://ouijit.com/faq/): Frequently asked questions about platform support, agent integrations, sandbox behavior.
- [GitHub repo](https://github.com/ouijit/ouijit): Source code, releases, issues.
- [Latest release](https://github.com/ouijit/ouijit/releases/latest): macOS (arm64/x64) DMG installers and Linux (x64) zipped binaries.

## Notable behavior for agents

- The `ouijit` CLI is available in every Ouijit-spawned terminal and authenticated by a per-session bearer token. It writes JSON to stdout; errors are `{"error": "..."}` on stderr with a non-zero exit.
- Every Ouijit terminal sets `OUIJIT_API_URL`, `OUIJIT_API_TOKEN`, and `OUIJIT_PTY_ID`; task terminals and hooks also get `OUIJIT_TASK_NUMBER`. Every `[pty-id]` argument defaults to `OUIJIT_PTY_ID`, so `task current`, `diff notes`, `tag`, `panel`, `runner`, `markdown`, `preview` and `link terminal` act on the agent's own terminal unless told otherwise. `OUIJIT_API_URL` is unset outside Ouijit terminals, so scripts can detect the environment.
- Status changes open a hook dialog in the GUI by default. In headless runs, pass `--run-hook`, `--skip-hook`, or `--hook-command "<cmd>"` to `task start`, `task create-and-start`, `task set-status`, and `task bulk-set-status`; `--sandbox host|nono|custom` overrides the hook's own sandbox for that run. `--surface terminal|chat` on `task start` and `task create-and-start` picks what the task opens in instead of the chat setting; a task Chat starts opens as a chat.
- `ouijit terminal list | read | open | paste | close` lets an agent read another terminal's screen, open a terminal in a task's worktree or the project, and paste text into a prompt. Paste never presses Enter; the user sends it. Opening a terminal never changes what the user is looking at.
- `ouijit ask run -- <command>` and `ouijit ask script <script>` ask the user to run something on this computer, outside any sandbox. The user reads the exact command and presses Run or Decline; nothing runs before that. With `--wait` the reply arrives when it finishes. The user may run it privately, in which case the agent gets only the exit code and `private: true`, and `panel read` of that runner returns only how it ended.
- `ouijit link diff|task|terminal|panel|pr|issue|board|project` prints an `ouijit://` URL. Put it in the reply as is; the user clicks it to go there. A link only navigates; nothing in Ouijit moves the user's view for an agent.
- `ouijit diff notes` returns the notes the user left on a worktree's diff, anchored to lines that stay current as the file changes.
- Tags belong to terminals, not tasks: `ouijit tag add|remove|clear <tag> [pty-id]` and `ouijit tag list` group terminals in the sidebar's Tags view. `ouijit task trash` replaces `task delete` and moves the worktree to the system trash.
- For pull request reviews, agents must stage comments locally with `ouijit pr draft add` (with `--origin <name>` and `--body -` for multi-line text) instead of posting with `gh`; the user sends the review from the app. Reading with `gh pr diff` is fine. Anchor comments to lines that appear as added lines in the diff, by new-file line number: one bad anchor makes GitHub reject the whole review.
- Under nono the terminal runs on the host, so the `ouijit` CLI shim stays on PATH at the project's CLI access level: read only (its own task, diff notes, links, asks, PR and Linear reads and drafts, and this terminal's tags and panels), its own task (also status, name and description changes to that task, linking a PR or issue to it, and creating to-do cards), or everything. Anything above the level is Forbidden, and the error names the `ouijit ask` that would run it outside the sandbox. PR and Linear drafts written from a sandbox are stamped with a `sandbox` origin, and a hook move from a sandbox waits in the user's queue even with `--run-hook`. The custom backend gets the same sandbox-scoped token as nono, but whether the `ouijit` CLI is reachable at all is the launcher's call.
- Claude Code, Codex, and Pi wrappers inject the CLI reference into the agent's system prompt, so agents can drive Ouijit (create tasks, flip statuses, manage hooks and scripts, read and paste into other terminals, tag terminals, stage PR drafts, switch themes, open runner, markdown and web preview panels) from the shell. OpenCode gets the same CLI reference, injected via the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var rather than a system-prompt flag.
